get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a **paginated** list of package credit types.

A package credit type links a credit type to a package and carries the credit `amount` granted for that package. The response is a standard paginated envelope: the records are in `data[]` (each item is `id`, `credit_type_id`, `package_id`, `amount`), alongside pagination metadata (`current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, `from`, `to`, `links`, and the `*_page_url` fields).

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field (see Filterable fields below). |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `credit_type_id` | integer (credit type) | `filter[credit_type_id][equal]=1` |
| `package_id` | integer (package) | `filter[package_id][equal]=24` |
| `amount` | number | `filter[amount][greater_than_equal]=1000` |

In practice the endpoint filters and sorts on any existing column. With no `sort`, results default to newest-first (by `id`).

The trailing path segment sets the data-detail level (e.g. `/credit_type_package/list/1`); it is optional for this entity and does not change the returned records — it is only echoed back into the pagination URLs.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of credit charges for the account. A credit charge is an amount of a given credit type granted to a client (e.g. loyalty points, prepaid credit, or a membership allowance) that is later consumed.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. `/credit_charge/list` and `/credit_charge/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[client_id][equal]=8` or `filter[status][equal]=available`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[amount]=desc`. |

**Filterable fields.** The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `staff_id` | integer (staff) | `filter[staff_id][equal]=1` |
| `client_id` | integer (client) | `filter[client_id][equal]=8` |
| `credit_type_id` | integer (credit type) | `filter[credit_type_id][equal]=1` |
| `status` | enum (`available`, `consumed`, `expired`, `suspended`) | `filter[status][equal]=available` |
| `start_date` | date | `filter[start_date][greater_than_equal]=2025-01-01` |
| `expiry_date` | date | `filter[expiry_date][less_than_equal]=2026-12-31` |
| `amount` | number | `filter[amount][greater_than]=10` |

The list will in fact filter and sort on any existing column, not only the fields above. When no `sort` is given the default ordering is newest first (`id` descending).

Each item in `data` is a flat credit-charge record. The `status` value is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `available` | Credit is available to consume |
| `consumed` | Credit has been fully used |
| `expired` | Credit passed its expiry date |
| `suspended` | Credit is temporarily suspended |

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing credit charge. This posts to the same `/v2/api/entity/credit_charge` path as create; the record to update is identified by the **`id` in the request body**. If `id` is omitted a new record is created instead.

**Important — this is a destructive partial overwrite, not a merge.** The update always rewrites a fixed **core set** of columns — `staff_id`, `client_id`, `credit_type_id`, `renewal_id`, and `amount` — and sets any of them **that you omit to null**. Because `client_id`, `credit_type_id`, and `amount` are non-nullable, omitting them fails with a `400`; omitting `staff_id` or `renewal_id` silently clears them. **Always resend the whole core set on every update.** The remaining fields (`start_date`, `expiry_date`, `description`, `status`) are preserved if omitted.

Date fields accept `YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD/MM/YYYY`. On success the response is `{ "message": <localized text>, "id": <id> }`.

client_id.description: Id of the client. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is nulled (→ 400).

credit_type_id.description: Id of the credit type. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is nulled (→ 400).

amount.description: Credit amount. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is nulled (→ 400).

staff_id.description: Id of the staff member. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is silently cleared to null.

renewal_id.description: Id of the membership renewal. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is silently cleared to null.

start_date.description: Start of the validity window. Optional; preserved if omitted. Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD/MM/YYYY`.

expiry_date.description: End of the validity window. Optional; preserved if omitted. Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD/MM/YYYY`.

description.description: Free-text note. Optional; preserved if omitted.

status.description:
Credit charge status. Optional; preserved if omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| available | Credit is available to consume |
| consumed | Credit has been fully used |
| expired | Credit passed its expiry date |
| suspended | Credit is temporarily suspended |

id.description: Id of the updated credit charge.

MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing **credit type**.

The record to update is identified by the **`id` field in the request body** (not by a path segment). Include `id` and POST to `/v2/api/entity/credit_type` — the same path as create; supplying `id` switches the operation from insert to update.

**This is a full-row overwrite.** Any writable field omitted from the body is reset to its column default or null (`status`→`1`, `allow_decimal`→`0`, `unit`/`description`→null), so always resend every field you want to keep. `name` is required and must stay **unique**.

Note: a request that puts the id in the path instead (`/credit_type/{id}`) does **not** update — it creates a new record. Always send `id` in the body.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | No |
| 1 | Yes |

status.description:
Optional. Whether the credit type is active. If omitted it resets to `1` (Active).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Inactive |
| 1 | Active |

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of packages (membership and credit-charge packages) for the account.

### Ordering
Newest first — `id` descending — unless you pass a `sort` parameter.

### Branch scoping
When the Branches add-on is enabled, results are automatically limited to your current branch. To widen the scope:

| Goal | How |
|---|---|
| A specific branch | `request_branch_id=<branch id>` |
| Every branch you have access to | `filter[branch_id][equal]=-1` |

Packages stored without a branch are not returned while branch scoping is in effect.

### Deleted packages
Deleted packages are excluded, so `deleted_at` is always `null` in this response. Fetch a deleted package directly by its id if you need it.

### Filtering
Use `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. Omitting the operator means `equal` — `filter[status]=1` is the same as `filter[status][equal]=1`.

| Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `equal` | equals (default) |
| `not_equal` | not equal |
| `in` / `not_in` | in / not in a list of values |
| `like` | partial text match |
| `gt` / `gte` / `from` | greater than / greater than or equal |
| `lt` / `lte` / `to` | less than / less than or equal |
| `is_null` / `is_not_null` | value is / is not empty |

Fields intended for filtering: `name`, `price`, `period_value`, `status`, `product_id`. Filtering on an unrecognised field returns `400`.

### Sorting
Use `sort[<field>]=asc` or `sort[<field>]=desc`, e.g. `sort[name]=asc`.

### Notes
- The trailing `1` in the path is an optional data-detail level. It has no effect for packages, which are always returned as flat records.
- A `fields[]` parameter is not supported; the complete record is always returned.

### Deleted packages
A deleted package is still returned by this endpoint, with `deleted_at` set to the time it was deleted. The list endpoint hides such packages, so this is the only place a non-null `deleted_at` appears.

No branch restriction applies here — a package belonging to any branch can be fetched by its id.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing package. The package is identified by the **`id` in the request body** — this endpoint uses the same URL as *Add New Package*.

### `id` selects the record
A body **without** `id` creates a new package instead of updating one, and still replies with an "Added Successfully" message. Always send `id`.

### Only the fields you send are changed — with two exceptions
Fields you leave out keep their current values. The exceptions are the two reference fields:

| Field | Left out of the body |
|---|---|
| `branch_id` | **Set to `null`** — the package loses its branch and stops appearing in *Get All Packages* |
| `product_id` | **Set to `null`** — the package is unlinked from its product |

So resend `branch_id` and `product_id` on every update, even when they are not changing.

### Clearing a text value
Sending `null` for `name`, `description`, `price`, `period_value`, `period_unit`, `status` or `type` leaves the current value untouched. Send an empty string (`""`) to clear a text field.

### Send `Accept: application/json`
This endpoint answers with a redirect to a web page instead of JSON when the request does not ask for JSON. Always send `Accept: application/json`.

### Other notes
- A successful update replies `Package Added Successfully` — the same wording as a create. Do not read it as proof that a new package was inserted; check the `id` you sent.
- An `id` that does not exist returns `400` with `"error": "Record Not Found"`, not `404`.
- Body keys that are not package fields are ignored silently — a misspelled field name is not reported as an error.
- `modified` is refreshed automatically; `created` and `deleted_at` should be omitted.
- Values are not validated against the lists below before they reach the database, so an out-of-range value fails as a save error rather than a field-level validation error.

The unit the validity period is counted in. Optional — unchanged when omitted.

| `daily` | Days |
| `weekly` | Weeks |
| `monthly` | Months |
| `yearly` | Years |
| `not-expired` | Never expires |

| Value | Meaning |

| `credit_charge` | A bundle of credits |
| `membership` | A membership subscription |
